key_insight: Concordat enforces agent action rules at runtime through typed, finite-state protocols rather than relying on prompt compliance.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can enforce confirmation gates, human-only decisions, and resource budgets before consequential tool calls take effect.
method: Expose only tools legal in the current protocol state and reject illegal calls before side effects.
Reserve designated decisions for humans and split token and tool-call budgets linearly across handoffs.
Check protocols at definition time and reject subclasses that could bypass inherited protocols.
evidence_signal: On tau-bench airline tasks with simulated pressure to skip confirmation, the standard agent violated confirmation rules in 13/50 GPT-4.1 tasks and 29/128 Claude Haiku 5.5 task-runs; Concordat had none, with no significant task-success difference.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to the reported airline evaluation; deployment still requires correctly specified protocols and coverage of consequential tool paths.
paper_title: Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents
